memory_update.text: The Consumer theme universe should prioritize second-order infrastructure over visible brands: retail trading-partner networks, B2B connectivity, logistics/trade compliance, product compliance/testing, private-label manufacturing, facility services, route density, contractor distribution, and niche component suppliers.

Retail EDI and trading-partner networks remain the highest-confidence chokepoint node because retailer-specific integrations, compliance logic, onboarding maps, and workflow embedding can create operational switching costs.

Testing, inspection, certification, product-data, labeling, and supplier-audit networks should be expanded in the next layer because regulatory and retailer-compliance complexity may be a durable consumer-infrastructure bottleneck.

Underfollowed consumer-adjacent names may sit in route-based services, private-label manufacturing, contractor distribution, local service networks, specialty components, and industrial materials rather than consumer GICS sectors.

Layer 2 should verify latest filings, market caps, analyst coverage, segment revenue, recurring revenue, customer concentration, organic versus acquisition growth, and valuation expectations before any candidate survives the funnel.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for the broad Consumer theme using the Serenity chokepoint lens. The highest-priority candidates are not consumer-facing brands but second-order infrastructure assets: retail trading-partner networks, B2B/EDI connectivity, logistics/trade compliance, retail execution software, product-data/compliance/testing, availability-driven component suppliers, facility/service networks, private-label and outsourced consumer manufacturing, and consumer-adjacent equipment/service distribution. The universe intentionally balances reference leaders with underfollowed or niche public companies; many smaller names remain hypotheses pending latest filings, market-cap checks, customer-dependency mapping, and segment-level revenue validation.
